Bigger frames and higher frame rates use more USB bandwidth, more WiFi and more CPU on the PC. On a shared hub they can cause dropped frames, freezes or extra latency, and the camera may not reach the frame rate it advertises. Go back to Automatic if anything breaks.
Before pointing a DIY camera at your eyes

Tracker Bridge cannot tell whether a USB camera is safe to point at your eyes.

Some DIY camera modules come with infrared LEDs that are too strong, or too close to the eye, for continuous use. The EyeTrackVR and Project Babble communities advise against the GC0308 IR module for eye tracking in particular: users report eye pain and dryness, and long infrared exposure is linked to lens damage over time.

Only point a camera at your eyes if you know its illumination is safe for that, such as the official EyeTrackVR or Project Babble builds. A camera used for mouth or face tracking does not have this problem.

By continuing you confirm that you understand the risk and that the hardware you use is your own responsibility.
